title: URL fetcher without allowlist
text: A parameter that supplies a URL, hostname, or webhook is fetched server-side with no allowlist. Typical path: image/PDF/preview fetchers, OAuth/OIDC discovery, XML/SVG parsers. Impact: read cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) for credentials, reach internal services, scan the internal network. Check for scheme/host allowlisting and whether redirects are followed.

title: Blocklist and redirect bypass
text: SSRF 'fixes' that blocklist localhost/127.0.0.1 are bypassed via alternate IP encodings (decimal, octal, IPv6, 0x7f.1), DNS rebinding, or an open redirect chained into the fetch. A one-time host check before a request that follows redirects is still vulnerable. Prefer a strict allowlist and disable redirects.

title: String-built SQL
text: User input concatenated or format-stringed into a SQL statement instead of bound parameters. Watch ORM raw/extra/literal escape hatches and dynamic ORDER BY/table/column names. Impact: auth bypass, data exfiltration, sometimes RCE via stacked queries or file writes. Safe form: bound placeholders and allowlisted identifiers.

title: Second-order SQLi
text: Input stored safely, then later concatenated into SQL at a different code path. The sink and source are separated in time/files, so single-file review misses it. Trace stored values to later query construction.

title: Object access without ownership check
text: A handler fetches or mutates a resource by an id/uuid/filename from the request but never verifies the current principal owns it. Sequential ids make enumeration trivial. Impact: read/modify other users' data. Safe form: scope queries to the authenticated user or assert permission before access.

title: AuthN present but AuthZ missing
text: A login (authentication) check exists, which looks protective, but there is no authorization check tying the object to the user. Also watch mass assignment where a user can set owner_id. The guard being present is what makes this subtle.

title: User input as template source
text: User input becomes part of the template SOURCE (render_template_string, Template(x).render(), f-string/concat building template text) rather than being passed as a context variable. Probe {{7*7}}. Jinja2 escalates to RCE via object traversal. Safe form: fixed template, input passed as bound data.

title: Shell with user input
text: User input reaches a shell (subprocess with shell=True, os.system, os.popen) by concatenation. Impact: arbitrary command execution. Safe form: pass an argument list without a shell, or strictly validate against an allowlist. shlex.quote helps but argument lists are safer.

title: Unsanitized path join
text: A filename/path from the request is joined to a base directory without containment, allowing ../ traversal to arbitrary files (/etc/passwd, source, secrets). Impact: local file read/inclusion. Safe form: basename + allowlist, or resolve and verify the path stays within the base directory.

title: Reflected/stored XSS
text: User input rendered into HTML/JS without contextual output encoding or with autoescaping disabled (|safe, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML). Impact: session theft, account takeover, actions as the victim. Safe form: contextual escaping and a Content-Security-Policy.

title: Committed credentials
text: API keys, tokens, passwords, or private keys written literally in source or config and committed. Impact: direct compromise of the associated service; often found in history even after removal. Safe form: load from environment or a secret manager; rotate anything exposed.

title: Unsafe deserialization
text: Untrusted data passed to pickle.loads, yaml.load (non-safe), or marshal. Impact: remote code execution via crafted gadget chains. Safe form: use data-only formats (JSON), yaml.safe_load, and never deserialize attacker-controlled bytes.
